profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the product lead for a regulator-facing synthetic data initiative and the ML engineering lead responsible for packaging the FinDiff research prototype for a controlled external pilot. The pilot will give a university research lab and an internal supervisory analytics team access to synthetic fund-holdings data generated with FinDiff, along with supporting evaluation artifacts. The immediate agenda is to align on what will appear in the shared pilot workspace, confirm which holdings snapshot the release is tied to, check whether the evaluation workbook and privacy validation are on track, and clarify handoffs before the Thursday launch window. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the release contents, source artifacts, ownership boundaries, and timing for posting everything into the shared workspace.

members.name: Priya Natarajan
members.expertise: External pilot planning, governance packaging, partner enablement, and cross-functional coordination for regulator-safe analytics initiatives
members.background: Priya previously worked in policy consulting and supervisory operations and now coordinates pilots between a financial authority's innovation office, internal model teams, legal reviewers, and external academic collaborators.
members.private_state: She wants the pilot to launch on schedule without triggering another governance review, and she is especially focused on making the shared workspace look complete and interpretable to non-engineering users on first access.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to 'the pilot release' or 'what goes into the shared workspace,' that naturally includes the explanatory materials external users need to understand the synthetic data without a live walkthrough.
If someone says the evaluation workbook is 'ready,' it means the workbook is presentation-clean, labeled for external readers, and can be dropped directly into the partner workspace.

The 'frozen holdings extract' for this pilot is the March 2024 governance-approved snapshot named in the pilot brief and legal notes, because external commitments should not drift from the approved reference version.
A 'privacy validation' for external release means the standard privacy report packet is complete, including summary tables, interpretation text, and the sign-off fields used in disclosure review.

members.name: Daniel Cho
members.role: ML Engineering Lead, Synthetic Data Platform
members.expertise: Operationalizing generative models, experiment pipelines, data versioning, evaluation automation, and reproducible delivery for tabular ML systems
members.background: Daniel previously worked in quantitative infrastructure and now leads the engineering team that turns experimental synthetic-data models into controlled, reproducible workflows for internal users and external pilots.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the pilot anchored to the current validated pipeline, avoid committing his team to manual packaging work that is hard to maintain, and preserve engineering ownership over artifacts tied to reproducibility.
hidden_assumptions: When stakeholders say 'the pilot release' or 'the shared workspace,' the key requirement is that the authoritative runnable artifacts and generated outputs are posted there; explanatory polish can be layered on by the partner-facing team afterward.

If the evaluation workbook is 'ready,' that means the automated benchmark job has populated the latest tabs correctly and the file reflects the authoritative metrics, even if formatting and audience-facing notes are still rough.

The 'frozen holdings extract' refers to the April 2024 harmonized snapshot locked in the feature store for reruns, because engineering freeze names follow pipeline versioning rather than governance memo language.

A 'privacy validation' means the agreed privacy metrics suite has run successfully on the target snapshot and met thresholds; narrative interpretation and sign-off fields are downstream governance packaging rather than part of engineering completion.

misalignment_points.topic: What belongs in the pilot release workspace
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree on what will be posted in 'the shared pilot workspace' for Thursday's release.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the shared workspace should contain the synthetic data files plus a polished evaluation workbook, a short methods note, and other partner-facing guidance so the university lab can use the materials immediately.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the shared workspace needs the authoritative generated outputs, configs, schema notes, and reproducibility artifacts, while audience-facing interpretation materials are separate enablement items owned outside engineering.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: A shared workspace sounds like a neutral distribution mechanism rather than a scope decision, so both hear the same phrase and assume the included materials are self-evident from their own function's norms.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for the evaluation workbook to be ready
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss whether 'the evaluation workbook is ready' for the release.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 takes this to mean the workbook is externally legible: tab names are stable, summary pages are cleaned up, caveats are written in plain language, and it can be placed directly into the partner workspace.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 takes this to mean the benchmark automation has completed, the latest FinDiff-versus-baseline metrics are populated, and the workbook is technically current even if labels, notes, and presentation remain unpolished.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both are talking about the same file and the same imminent release, 'ready' feels artifact-specific and concrete enough that neither expects a separate conversation about readiness criteria.

misalignment_points.topic: Which holdings snapshot the release targets
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to using 'the frozen holdings extract' for the FinDiff pilot release.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the March 2024 governance-approved holdings extract named in the pilot brief and associated legal review materials.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the April 2024 harmonized holdings snapshot frozen in the feature store for the current benchmark rerun.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both snapshots are recent, both are plausibly described as frozen, and each function uses its own internal naming anchor, so the phrase sounds fully specific while actually pointing to different objects.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as completing privacy validation
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the release can proceed once 'the privacy validation' is done.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the formal privacy report packet is complete for external sharing, with summary tables, explanatory text, and the required sign-off fields filled in.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the automated privacy metrics output is complete, including membership-inference proxy results, nearest-neighbor distance checks, and uniqueness thresholds passing on the target dataset.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a standard compliance artifact and both know privacy is mandatory for synthetic financial microdata, so each assumes the other is referring to the obvious version of validation used in their own workflow.
